summary: Rhode Island enacted AI companion-chatbot safety and AI-in-mental-health laws in June 2026, which address chatbot harms rather than catastrophic risk. AG Peter Neronha co-signed the Sept 2026 state-AG letter urging federal frontier-AI rules.

items.title: S 2195/H 7350 — AI companion chatbot safeguards
items.text: Requires chatbot suicide/self-harm detection, periodic AI disclosure and annual reports to the Attorney General.

items.title: 26-AG letter to Congress on frontier AI safety
items.text: The Rhode Island attorney general signed the letter urging Congress to adopt federal frontier-AI safety rules and to bar preemption of state AI laws.

profile.headline: Rhode Island is focused on using AI inside state government, with a task force roadmap and a federally funded AI institute at Brown.

sections.text: Gov. Dan McKee's Executive Order 24-06 (February 2024) created an AI Task Force chaired by former Rep. Jim Langevin. Its January 2026 roadmap recommended AI workforce training, state-service pilots, a central AI guidance body and an AI-RI collaboration hub.
Brown University leads ARIA, a $20 million NSF AI research institute announced July 2025 and led by Ellie Pavlick, developing trustworthy AI assistants with mental-health care as the target use.
Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, with Sens. Van Hollen and Heinrich, opened an inquiry on March 13, 2026 into eight companies including Meta, OpenAI and xAI over gas-powered data-center projects.

No large AI data center has been built or approved in Rhode Island. The main proposal is a business complex with a data center near the Fidelity campus in Smithfield. It is backed by Hanton City Investments LLC, a partnership that includes Revity Energy's Ryan Polumbo, and projects $59 million in revenue for the town over 30 years. The developer filed its application on May 4, 2026.

On May 5, 2026, the Smithfield Town Council voted 4-1 to bar data centers from every zoning district. Residents raised concerns about noise, water, electricity and conservation land. Because the Hanton City application was filed a day earlier, it may still be reviewed under the old rules. At the state level, six data-center bills were introduced in the 2026 session and none cleared committee.
